name: qualified-label-parens
why: Credential label has a parenthesized qualifier before the separator, so a strict name-separator matcher may miss it.

name: qualified-label-brackets
why: Credential label has a bracketed qualifier between the name and separator.

name: qualified-label-slash
why: Credential name is followed by a slash qualifier before the separator.

name: git-config-quoted-subsection
why: Credential appears as a generic value inside a git-config subsection whose credential meaning is in the quoted subsection.

name: html-data-credential-attr
why: HTML stores the credential name and value in data-* attributes rather than name/id/http-equiv plus value/content.

name: html-aria-label-password
why: Credential cue appears in aria-label with the secret in a value attribute.

name: html-placeholder-cue
why: Credential cue appears only in placeholder text, not name/id/http-equiv.

name: yaml-sequence-pair
why: YAML expresses a credential pair as name/value objects in a sequence.

name: yaml-flow-object-name-value
why: YAML flow object uses generic name/value keys, with the credential cue in the name value.

name: json-name-value-pair
why: JSON uses a generic name/value object rather than a credential key.

name: json-env-array-pair
why: Container env arrays commonly store credential names and values in separate fields.

name: toml-array-of-tables-name-value
why: TOML stores env var credentials as name/value entries, not credential keys.

name: ini-name-value-object
why: INI section is generic and the credential cue is a value of name, with the secret under generic value.

name: properties-indexed-env
why: Indexed property path hides the credential name in a previous sibling field.

name: spring-relaxed-binding-brackets
why: Spring-style indexed properties split name and value across sibling keys.

name: dotenv-array-name-value
why: (was held only) Dotenv-like indexed name/value variables keep the credential cue separate from the value variable.

name: python-dict-name-value
why: Python code uses generic name/value keys in a dict.

name: python-click-option-default
why: CLI option declares password semantics while the secret is in a default argument.

name: javascript-object-label-value
why: JavaScript object stores a credential label and generic value field.

name: go-struct-tag-env
why: Go struct tag identifies the env credential, but the value is in a generic Default field.
input: type Config struct { Secret string `env:"PASSWORD" default:"CorrectHorse9!"` }

name: java-annotation-default
why: Java annotation value has credential semantics in one attribute and secret in another.

name: csharp-attribute-name-value
why: C# attribute stores credential name and generic default separately.

name: php-array-name-value
why: PHP array uses name/value fields rather than a credential key.

name: ruby-hash-name-value
why: Ruby hash separates the credential cue from the generic value field.

name: rust-attribute-env-default
why: Rust config attribute names the credential env var and stores secret in a generic default.

name: url-path-key-value
why: Credential cue and value are encoded as path segments.

name: graphql-variable-name-value
why: GraphQL variables use generic input object fields with credential cue in a name field.

name: graphql-directive-default
why: GraphQL directive carries credential name and generic default separately.

name: protobuf-text-name-value
why: Protobuf text format uses repeated name/value entries rather than credential keys.

name: ansible-vars-name-value
why: Ansible list of vars stores credential variable name and value as separate keys.

name: helm-set-json-array
why: Helm --set-json carries name/value objects inside a quoted command argument.

name: plist-key-string
why: Apple plist stores key and value in adjacent XML elements instead of a credential tag containing text.
